nodes.name: Read Recent from MySQL
nodes.notes: Selects rows from the MySQL table (returnAll) — the read side of the store. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Newest First
nodes.notes: Orders items (newest first) so limits and digests pick the most relevant records.

nodes.name: Trim to Digest Size
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 15 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Content (AI)
nodes.notes: Map-reduce summarization chain — handles long content without blowing the context window.

nodes.name: OpenAI Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: gpt-4o-mini). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenAI API key. platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.

nodes.name: Post Digest to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#inbox-ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Archive Digest in MySQL
nodes.notes: Inserts a row into the MySQL table using fields auto-mapped from the incoming item. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: MySQL connection. Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

# Send a metrics report with MySQL

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers newsletters work end to end across MySQL and Slack.

It moves through 9 working steps, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Recent from MySQL
3. Newest First
4. Trim to Digest Size
5. Summarize Content (AI)
6. OpenAI Chat Model
7. Post Digest to Slack
8. Archive Digest in MySQL
9. Stamp Processing Time

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Recent from MySQL → Newest First → Trim to Digest Size → Summarize Content (AI) → OpenAI Chat Model → Post Digest to Slack → Archive Digest in MySQL → Stamp Processing Time

## Use it for

- Teams keeping MySQL and Slack aligned by hand for newsletters
- Newsletters work where "Read Recent from MySQL" is still a manual step before MySQL
- Newsletters work that only reaches MySQL on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps MySQL and Slack in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed MySQL or Slack call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 9 nodes in this newsletters build
- The newsletters AI step is isolated from MySQL, so models swap without touching the other 9 nodes
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 9 nodes for newsletters before wiring MySQL
- 9 nodes, each with a doc card explaining what it does for newsletters

## Before first run
Connect credentials: MySQL connection; OpenAI API key; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Summarization uses a Chain, not an Agent, because the step is fixed — there's no decision about which tool to call, just 'summarize this text.' Posting to multiple channels runs as parallel branches, not sequential sends, so a slow API on one channel never delays the message that was already ready on another.

## Practice exercises

New to this pattern? Try these in order:

1. Add a third notification channel and watch the Merge node's input count update.
2. Change 'Trim to Digest Size' from 15 to 5 and see how it narrows the summary's scope.
3. Swap the Summarization Chain for a Q&A Chain to answer questions instead of just recapping.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**MySQL connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your MySQL provider.
_Gotcha:_ Remote access often needs the n8n server's IP allow-listed.

**OpenAI API key**
platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.
_Gotcha:_ Needs billing set up; a brand-new key with no credit returns 429 immediately.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 When this fails

This starter workflow keeps things simple: no automatic retry or error branch yet. If a node fails, the execution just stops — open n8n's **Executions** tab to see which node and why. Ready to harden it? Turn on **Retry On Fail** (3 tries, 2s backoff) on the Settings tab of each external node, and add an error-output branch to a Slack/email alert — every Production-tier template in this library shows that exact pattern.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- MySQL: grant the user only the tables this workflow touches; avoid `GRANT ALL` on the schema.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
newsletters payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
